Ghomala'

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Rhymes: -a

Verb

[edit]

pá (transitive) alternate of bá

  1. to treat, to cure
    Ě pá fípa. ― He/she cured the fever.
  2. to spy, to watch
    Tâmbɛ̂ yə̂ŋ pá á. ― This gentleman spies on me.
  3. to stick, to attach
    Ê pá mnwə myə̀ nə̂ m. ― He/she sticks her stories to me.
  4. to plant
    Ě pá ŋkədé. ― He/she planted a banana.

Irish

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • pádh (obsolete)
  • páí (Cois Fharraige)

Etymology

[edit]

From Old French paie (“payment, recompense”), from paiier (“to pay”), from Latin pācō (“I settle, satisfy, pacify”), from pāx (“peace”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Munster, Connacht) IPA(key): /pˠɑː/
  • (Ulster) IPA(key): /pˠæː/

Noun

[edit]

pá m or f (genitive singular pá, nominative plural pánna)

  1. pay, wages (money given in return for work)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of pá (fourth declension)
bare forms
singular plural
nominative pá pánna
vocative a phá a phánna
genitive pá pánna
dative pá pánna
forms with the definite article
singular plural
nominative an pá na pánna
genitive an phá na bpánna
dative leis an bpá
don phá 		leis na pánna

Derived terms

[edit]
  • fear pá (“paid workman”)
  • íosphá, pá íosta (“minimum wage”)
  • lá pá (“pay-day”)

Mutation

[edit]
Mutated forms of pá
radical lenition eclipsis
pá phá bpá

Old Tupi

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • pa (obsolete)

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpa/
  • Rhymes: -a
  • Hyphenation: pá

Etymology 1

[edit]

Particle

[edit]

pá

  1. (men's speech) yes
    Synonyms: eẽ, hẽhẽ, îé
    Antonym: aan
    — Ereîukápe?
    — Pá, îagûarera aîuká.
    — Did you kill it?
    — Yes, I killed the jaguar.

Etymology 2

[edit]

Determiner

[edit]

pá

  1. all; every
    Aîybõmbá
    I've shoot them all

Adverb

[edit]

pá

  1. totally; completely
    Ereroŷrõmbápe sekó?
    Do you hate his works completely?

Further reading

[edit]
  • Navarro, Eduardo de Almeida (2013), “pá”, in Dicionário de tupi antigo: a língua indígena clássica do Brasil [Dictionary of Old Tupi: The Classical Indigenous Language of Brazil ] (overall work in Portuguese), São Paulo: Global, →ISBN, page 367, column 1

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpa/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈpa/

  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
  • Homophone: par (non-rhotic accents)
  • Rhymes: -a
  • Hyphenation: pá

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese paa, from Latin pālam (“shovel”). Doublet of pala. Compare Galician pa and Spanish pala.

Noun

[edit]

pá f (plural pás)

  2. shovel; spade (tool for digging and moving material)
  4. windmill blade
  6. the end of a paddle or oar with the blade
  8. (Portugal) shoulder, chuck (cut of meat)

Etymology 2

[edit]

Shortening of rapaz (“boy”),[1] from earlier paz.

Noun

[edit]

pá m (uncountable)

  2. (Portugal, informal, used in the vocative) dude; mate (term of informal address)
    Synonyms: (Brazil) cara, mano, (Brazil) rapá, (Brazil) bróder
    Estás bom, pá? ― You alright, dude?
    Ó pá, aonde vais? ― Hey man, where are you going?

Interjection

[edit]

pá

  2. (Portugal, informal) dude; man
    Ena, pá! ― Wow, dude!
Usage notes
[edit]
  • Despite derived from the masculine rapaz, the word is used for any gender.

Etymology 3

[edit]

Onomatopoeic.

Interjection

[edit]

pá

  1. bam, boom
    Resolvemos uns assuntos e pá! ― We finished some discussion and bam!

Etymology 4

[edit]

Preposition

[edit]

pá

  1. (nonstandard, colloquial) contraction of para +‎ a

Etymology 5

[edit]

Particle

[edit]

pá

  1. (Brazil, colloquial, informal) Indicates aposiopesis.

Usage notes

[edit]

The element pá is used almost exclusively in a few set expressions:

  • "pode pá" ("you can...") — shortening of "pode crer" ("that's right"; literally "you can believe it")
  • "se pá" ("if...") — shortening of conditional expressions such as "se for o caso" ("if that's the case") or "se der" ("if it's possible")
  • "e pá" ("and...") — shortening of "e tal" ("and such")
  • "meio pá" ("kinda...") — indicates omission of negative adjectives denoting upsetness or disagreeability

References

[edit]
  1. ^ Carlos Marinheiro (16 November 2016 (last accessed)), “O uso de pá (vocativo e interjeição) em Portugal”, in Ciberdúvidas‎[1]

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pá”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “pá”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

Suyá

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Northern Jê *bə (“forest”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈpʌ]

Noun

[edit]

pá

  1. forest
    Hwĩsôsôk itha khãm kê wapatá me pá me ngô me hwykha me mbyt me khajkhwa me ithadjê ro sujarẽni.
    This book also discusses the importance of our villages, forests, rivers, lands, the sun and the sky.
